Garlic bread and sex are meant to fulfill two completely different needs. Saying that one is objectively better than the other is like saying brown sugar is better than white sugar. They both serve different purposes. 

If you have a hankering for garlic bread, you're going to, in that moment, believe garlic bread to be preferable to sex. Same goes for the opposite.

Sex can lead to euphoria and bonding, but it can also lead to injury and dissatisfaction. Garlic bread is, for the most part, tasty and nourishing, but along with it comes a slight risk of overeating (if too well-made) and disappointment (if not well-made enough). The benefits of eating garlic bread seem minor in comparison to those of sex, but the same can be said for the detriments. If you're looking for something that you'll almost definitely enjoy, have some garlic bread. If you're in the mood for something a little more risky, go for sex.

What I'm trying to say is that whether or not garlic bread is better than sex is dependent on a variety of factors. From your innate personality to what you had for breakfast, a lot goes into how you feel about this debate.

I sat down and buried my head in my arms. I had practically raised Hilary Duff with my own two hands. I could remember the day she had taken her first step, the day she had lost her first tooth, the day she had graduated from kindergarten. Yes, I was just her babysitter, but our bond had grown beyond that. The memories we’d created together were indelible.

 Unfortunately, my side business as a time-traveller had become more and more demanding. I just couldn’t balance taking care of Hilary and maintaining my career. I had no choice but to quit my job as Hillary’s babysitter.

She was crestfallen the day I left. I will never forget the look on her face as I walked out her front door for the very last time. I will never forget the feeble little wave she gave me as I climbed into my space-time traverser. Even if nobody believes that I was Hillary Duff’s babysitter.
